C03 and C12 share parts of this machinery, especially regret, gratitude, future assistance, and personal good wishes, but C04 is the closest overall drafting model.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I accept, as I must, your resignation ... effective January 20, 1961. I do so with real regret","parent_excerpt":"It is with great regret and reluctance that I accept your resignation ... effective on or about March fifteenth.","explanation":"Closely parallel opening machinery combining acceptance, effective date, and emphatic regret."},{"child_excerpt":"You have served not only with the utmost professional distinction but with a spirit of constructive helpfulness and outstanding dedication.","parent_excerpt":"You have devoted yourself tirelessly and selflessly ... I am grateful to you for your outstanding service.","explanation":"Both next commend the departing official’s exceptional dedication and service."},{"child_excerpt":"I especially appreciate your offer to continue to be available to me for future assistance.","parent_excerpt":"I am even more grateful for your assurance that, when circumstances might indicate a renewed need for your services, I would be free to call upon you.","explanation":"Distinctive shared provision acknowledging the departing official’s continuing availability for future service."},{"child_excerpt":"you take with you my very best wishes for a future as rewarding and productive","parent_excerpt":"Mrs. Eisenhower joins me in the hope that you and Mrs. Brundage will enjoy to the fullest, for many years, the happiness and satisfactions that you so richly deserve.","explanation":"Both close the substantive text with warm wishes for the recipient’s post-government future."}]}
